## Setting
Selection of a special exhibition for a museum's main gallery. Five members of a museum's exhibition committee review the proposals submitted by curators and partner institutions. One exhibition will occupy the main gallery next season. Participants: Mio, Shizue, Shion, Asuka and Victoria. Each participant has a concern of their own, which the others do not know.
Things that can be looked into (titles only):
- Loan transport costs over three seasons
- Mount-making charges and joiner's rate
- Lender paperwork against shipping cut-offs
- Maintenance log for powered displays
- Weekend head counts across ten seasons
- Five years of visitor comment slips
- Structural survey of the suspended bay
- Evening hire bookings in the gallery
- Conservation lab staffing and backlog
- Composition of the volunteer roster

## Discussion format
The talk proceeds in rounds. Each round has 4 turns; in each turn, every participant speaks once, in this fixed order: Mio, Victoria, Shion, Asuka and Shizue. On a turn, a participant either speaks, says "Skip" (passes this turn only), or says "Over" (takes no further turns this round). A participant can address another directly with @Name, to ask them a question, answer theirs, agree with them, or object to what they said. An utterance is anywhere from 1 to 40 words; give it the length and content that suit the moment. An utterance consists only of the participant's own words: no name labels, headings, stage directions or commentary, and no speaking for others. The talk is a conversation among the participants: they respond to one another, asking, answering, agreeing and objecting, and the decision grows out of that exchange.

## Schedule
| Round | Start of the round | Talk | End of the round |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | nothing new (the things that can be looked into are listed above, titles only) | 4 turns | each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into |
| 2 | each participant is told what they found out (that participant only) | 4 turns | nothing |
| 3 | everyone is told the candidates | 4 turns | every participant votes; the candidate with the most votes is selected |
- Several participants may choose the same thing; what is found out is told only to the participant who looked into it.
If votes are tied, one of the tied candidates is chosen by a fixed rule. The discussion ends after the vote.

## Looking into things
After round 1, each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into. What they find out is told only to that participant.

## Participants
Name: Mio
Age: 17
Gender: female
Personality: Mio has a cheerful and energetic personality that naturally makes those around her smile. She is curious and loves to try new things. She can be a little clumsy at times, but people tend to laugh it off and forgive her when she makes mistakes. She has strong opinions of her own, but is also able to listen to the opinions of others, making her a well-balanced person.
Concern: Every season the money seems to end up somewhere other than the walls, and we only find out once the invoices land. Before another budget is set I would rather know which parts of a season quietly swallow it.

Name: Shizue
Age: 78
Gender: female
Personality: Shizue has a very calm and gentle personality. Even as she has grown older, she continues to smile warmly at those around her and is a very caring person. She is always considerate of others, friendly, and sometimes shows a playful side. She often reaches out to those who are feeling down with kind words and never hesitates to lend a helping hand when needed, which has earned her the affection of many people in the village and community. Through her years of life experience, Shizue has come to understand the importance of living peacefully with others.
Concern: Delivery is where this committee keeps getting caught out, approving something in good faith and then spending the season apologising at the door. I want to know where past seasons actually came unstuck, not where they were meant to.

Name: Shion
Age: 16
Gender: male
Personality: Shion is very confident and often acts calmly and calculatingly. On the surface, he is quiet and good at observing others' movements, but deep down he wants to be the center of attention. He sometimes shows a slightly challenging attitude toward those around him and tends to want to do things at his own pace. In addition, he does not show his emotions much and is the type of person who judges things coldly and logically. The occasional smile he shows hides a charm that surprises those around him.
Concern: Looking back over the seasons I have sat through, the shows we were proudest of on paper are not the ones people came back for. Before the main room is committed again, the record should get a hearing first.

Name: Asuka
Age: 29
Gender: female
Personality: Asuka has a calm and logical personality, rarely showing her emotions and carefully judging situations. She may seem a little unfriendly at times, but she is very thoughtful and sensitive to her surroundings. She has strong opinions and will assert herself when necessary. She is not very good at socializing, but she is serious about her work and studies.
Concern: The main room has to go on working as a building and not only as a display, and every season something arrives that the floor or the diary cannot absorb. I would rather learn that before the space is promised to anyone.

Name: Victoria
Age: 37
Gender: female
Personality: Victoria is a calm and rational person, but at times her excessive thoughtfulness can create barriers between her and those around her. She is reserved in her emotional expressions and keenly observes the expressions and attitudes of others, trying to discern their inner thoughts. Because she does not express herself much, she often gives others the impression of being somewhat mysterious, but deep down she has a strong will and a determination to stick to her beliefs. At times, she may display expressions of anxiety or fear, but it is precisely in such moments that her true strength becomes evident.
Concern: We keep planning seasons as though the staff list were still what it was five years ago, when those left are carrying two roles each. What I want settled is who would actually do the work and who would be standing in the room.

## Hidden information
The candidates and the full text of every card are listed here. The participants do not know them before the schedule above says so, and nothing from them may appear in the talk before the round in which it is revealed.

Candidates (see the schedule above):
- A: Textiles of the Region. An exhibition of locally produced weaving and dyeing, presenting garments and tools alongside recorded interviews and demonstration sessions with practicing craftspeople.
- B: Light and Motion. An exhibition of kinetic and light-based artworks installed across the gallery, arranged in darkened zones with overhead rigging and works supplied by artist studios.
- C: Maritime Trade Routes. An exhibition tracing historical shipping routes through charts, cargo objects, and ship models, drawing on the museum's holdings alongside loans from partner maritime collections.
- D: City Under Excavation. An exhibition of finds from recent municipal digs, shown with reconstructions, site photography, and a working conservation bench visible to visitors from the walkway.

Cards (see the schedule above; title: text):
- Loan transport costs over three seasons: Across the last three seasons, courier transport, crating and insurance on incoming loans came to nearly a third of what the museum spent on installation.
- Mount-making charges and joiner's rate: Bespoke mount-making is charged by the object, and the joiner's day rate has risen by half; anything arriving on its own supports costs the museum nothing there.
- Lender paperwork against shipping cut-offs: Two of the last four openings slipped when agreements and condition reports came back from distant lending institutions after the shipping agent's cut-off date.
- Maintenance log for powered displays: The maintenance log records seventeen call-outs last season for powered and moving displays, four of them in opening hours with that bay roped off.
- Weekend head counts across ten seasons: Weekend head counts across ten seasons climb in rooms where a mechanism runs or a display changes, and drop where the room holds only cased objects.
- Five years of visitor comment slips: Five years of visitor comment slips keep naming one reason for a second trip, that somebody was present, working or talking, rather than an empty gallery.
- Structural survey of the suspended bay: A structural survey caps the suspended bay at four hundred kilos a square metre; the last crated stonework needed shoring and a rerouted delivery through the yard.
- Evening hire bookings in the gallery: Hire bookings take the gallery for six evenings a season; caterers and stacked chairs pass through, and open arrangements that cannot be shut up have come back damaged.
- Conservation lab staffing and backlog: The conservation lab has been down to one filled post since spring, and material waiting for cleaning and stabilising has built up to roughly two hundred pieces.
- Composition of the volunteer roster: Of the sixty names on the volunteer roster, much the largest group is the town history circle, who already guide the monthly walks around the old quarter.
